raw.assessment: The incumbent offers a plausible opportunity to check completeness and fit during assembly, while removable slots retain rearrangeability; these benefits are not causally demonstrated. Performance remains insufficient: median combined time is 11 minutes, five partition problems were reported, and seven of ten observed customers succeeded unaided. D2-O6 limits an account that full assembly inherently takes too long: repeated three-compartment orders took seven to nine minutes, while every extreme delay occurred in mixed batches. Layout complexity and switching remain confounded. No damage claims alone cannot establish packaging effectiveness.

openings.claim: Order-specific reusable parts trays may reduce selection and checking delays and partition omissions while retaining full workshop assembly.
openings.delta: Separate each accepted order’s required parts and exterior color before insertion instead of selecting repeatedly from shared shape bins.
openings.prediction: Against the incumbent on matched mixed-layout runs, selection/checking time and independently counted kit errors decrease without a comparable insertion-time change.
openings.probe: Using reusable sample parts within the 15-sample allowance, alternate incumbent and tray runs across both workers and accepted layout/color variants. Time selection, insertion, checking and packing separately, including tray preparation; independently inventory every completed kit. Check total cost and delivery impact before pilot adoption.
assumptions: Trays can be made within 500 initially and 0.40 recurring per order.
Trials fit available working time; ordered components, footprint, capacity, removability and colors remain identical.

openings.claim: Does locating the short partition in the ordered layout, rather than physical insertion difficulty, explain the observed requests for help?
openings.delta: Replace the generic three-layout diagram with an order-specific diagram clearly locating the short partition.
openings.prediction: If layout interpretation is limiting, correct unaided short-partition placement improves while insertion retries after correct positioning remain similar.
openings.probe: Assign ten participants to matched layout groups receiving either diagram with otherwise identical organizers. Observe placement decisions, insertion retries, requests for help and successful ordered arrangement within ten minutes. Treat this as a small diagnostic, not proof of 90% pilot success.
assumptions: The replacement diagram fits the existing print allowance and delivery schedule.
Equivalent physical parts and balanced layouts make the comparison interpretable.

raw.assessment: The observations establish slow mixed batches and arrangement difficulties, but do not isolate selection, insertion or packing causes. One hybrid hypothesis merits a bounded test; feasibility and customer benefit remain unproved.

openings.claim: Shared shape bins may generate repeated identity-and-count reconciliation as orders change; full workshop assembly may add insertion work without reliably teaching customers partition placement. Hypothesized feedback: these organizing choices increase checking, correction and explanation demand. Replace full assembly with an order-specific mapped kit.
openings.delta: Counterfactual branch: forbid full workshop assembly. Hybrid parents are a parts-completeness witness and a placement guide: each required partition occupies a labeled outline on a packing card, and the same label identifies its location in the ordered-layout diagram. Their interaction makes one interface support packing verification and customer placement. Former assembly obligations are structural-fit checking, completeness, correct layout, stability and presentation. Replace them with reversible fit checks, a filled-card check, matched labels, a customer stability check and a restrained presentation pack; retain ordered counts, exterior color and rearrangeability.
openings.prediction: Against matched incumbent orders, mapped kits should reduce selection corrections and workshop insertion time without increasing customer placement errors. If only insertion time falls, the shared-bin feedback hypothesis lacks support. Faster packing accompanied by more customer errors rejects the proposed hybrid.
openings.probe: Use spare board for matched samples across all compartment counts; separately time selection, fit checking, assembly and packing, counting corrections. Randomly allocate the ten participants between incumbent and mapped-kit unpacking for an exploratory error comparison. Verify loaded footprint, dismantling, color and costs before adoption. The unchanged 60-unit pilot must achieve at least 59 complete orders, median workshop time at most eight minutes and at least 90% unaided arrangement; the small exploration cannot establish those rates.
assumptions: Replacement dependencies: accurate order-to-parts mapping; legible removable or unobtrusive labels; correct placement diagram; reliable fit and stability checks; restraint preventing parts escaping their mapped positions; customer assembly ability.
Cards, labels, preparation and checks must fit the 500 initial and 0.40 recurring cost limits and fixed delivery date; this is unmeasured.
The sales description permits supplied unassembled partitions; customer acceptance is unmeasured.

critiques.assumption: Removing full workshop assembly releases useful time without losing a necessary fit-and-completeness check.
critiques.limitation: D2-O2 does not separate activities; D2-O5 records insertion retries. Neither establishes that replacement fit checks are cheaper or equally effective. Forbidding full assembly is a strategy choice, not a case constraint.
critiques.opening: Retain assembly while testing the mapped-kit information mechanism, then isolate the additional effect of removing assembly.
critiques.comparison: A linked assembled organizer may deliver the identity-transfer benefit with less customer insertion burden, but retains workshop insertion time.
critiques.probe: Compare linked assembled and linked unassembled samples with identical parts, diagrams and independent final inventories; include every replacement check in workshop time.

critiques.assumption: Order-specific completeness and placement representations are correct and remain aligned.
critiques.limitation: A wrong order-to-parts mapping can make a filled card and matching diagram agree while the delivered arrangement is wrong. Supplied observations do not measure this dependency.
critiques.opening: Check mapping against the accepted order independently before evaluating the interface.
critiques.comparison: Linking tray and diagram may reduce reconciliation, but also couples their errors; neither parent alone establishes mapping accuracy.
critiques.probe: Independently derive required counts, color and positions from accepted orders and compare them with proposed maps.

openings.claim: An order-linked tray and placement diagram may improve both workshop checking and customer arrangement while retaining full assembly.
openings.delta: Give each tray position a corresponding diagram identifier; preserve workshop assembly and use the linked information during final checking and unpacking.
openings.prediction: Beyond Z1, the diagram should improve placement; beyond Z2, the tray should reduce selection/checking errors. Their proposed interaction is reuse of one component identity across packing and unpacking. Against A1, customer insertion burden should decrease while workshop insertion remains. Incorrect maps or labels losing their referent break this interaction.
openings.probe: Within 15 samples, allocate three each to incumbent, Z1, Z2, linked assembled and A1; cover all compartment counts and include rare color. Time all preparation/checking stages. Use ten participants in five matched-layout pairs comparing the linked assembled and A1 versions, without prior practice. These proposed diagnostics cannot establish pilot success rates.
assumptions: Mapping and identifiers remain interpretable after packing.
Footprint, assortment capacity, removable partitions, ordered counts and color remain intact.
Preparation, labels and trials fit 500 initially, 0.40 recurring and the fixed delivery date; feasibility is unmeasured.

openings.claim: Order trays may reduce selection/checking delay and omissions.
openings.discriminator: Selection/checking improves without comparable insertion change.
openings.probe: Compare trays with incumbent; include preparation and independent inventories.
openings.uncertainty: Switching and layout complexity remain confounded.

openings.claim: Ordered-layout diagrams may resolve short-partition confusion.
openings.discriminator: Correct placement improves while correctly positioned insertion retries persist.
openings.probe: Compare diagrams; observe placement, retries, help and ten-minute success.

openings.claim: Mapped unassembled kits combine completeness witnessing with placement guidance and remove workshop insertion.
openings.discriminator: Only insertion savings weaken reconciliation hypothesis; increased customer errors reject hybrid.
openings.probe: Compare linked assembled/unassembled samples; count replacement fit, stability, restraint and presentation checks in time.
openings.uncertainty: Check equivalence, label continuity, customer ability and acceptance unproved; assembly prohibition is optional.

openings.claim: Linked trays/diagrams may transfer component identity while retaining assembly.
openings.discriminator: Diagram adds placement benefit beyond trays; trays add checking benefit beyond diagrams.
openings.probe: Compare incumbent, trays, diagrams, linked assembled and mapped unassembled.
openings.uncertainty: Shared incorrect mapping can synchronize errors; identifiers may lose referents.

post_distill.decision: Independently derive mappings from accepted orders first. Explore three samples per five arms, both workers, all counts and rare color; ten customers in five matched pairs compare linked assembled/unassembled. Time every stage. Preserve 30x20 footprint, assortment, removable partitions, ordered counts/colors; verify 500 initial, 0.40 recurring and fixed date. Synthetic small diagnostics cannot establish pilot thresholds: 59/60 complete, median <=8 minutes, >=90% unaided.
